provenance: Human-authored from standard distributed-systems curriculum (networking, replication, consensus, consistency, messaging). Not derived from Synapse gold JSONL.
review_notes: Covers client-server, consensus, CAP/consistency, and queue-based async processing cases.

concepts.title: Networking Basics
concepts.description: Hosts, ports, packets, and basic end-to-end communication assumptions.

concepts.title: HTTP
concepts.description: Request/response application protocol commonly used by web clients and servers.

concepts.title: Client-Server
concepts.description: Architecture where clients request services from servers over a network.

concepts.title: APIs
concepts.description: Contracts that expose server capabilities to remote clients.

concepts.title: Distributed Systems Intro
concepts.description: Overview of systems composed of networked processes that cooperate.

concepts.title: Failure Models
concepts.description: Crash, omission, and Byzantine failure assumptions used in protocol design.

concepts.title: Replication
concepts.description: Maintaining copies of state across multiple nodes for availability and durability.

concepts.title: Paxos
concepts.description: Classic consensus protocol family for agreeing on values under failures.

concepts.title: Raft
concepts.description: Leader-based consensus algorithm designed for understandability.

concepts.title: Consensus
concepts.description: Agreement among nodes on a single value or log entry despite failures.

concepts.title: CAP Theorem
concepts.description: Trade-off framing among consistency, availability, and partition tolerance.

concepts.title: Eventual Consistency
concepts.description: Replicas may diverge temporarily but converge in the absence of updates.

concepts.title: Linearizability
concepts.description: Strong consistency model where operations appear instantaneous and ordered.

concepts.title: Consistency Models
concepts.description: Spectrum of guarantees describing how replicas expose shared state.

concepts.title: Producer-Consumer
concepts.description: Pattern separating work producers from work consumers via a buffer.

concepts.title: Message Queues
concepts.description: Durable or buffered channels that decouple senders and receivers.

concepts.title: Delivery Guarantees
concepts.description: At-most-once, at-least-once, and related delivery semantics for messaging.

concepts.title: Backpressure
concepts.description: Flow-control mechanisms that slow producers when consumers cannot keep up.

concepts.title: Async Processing
concepts.description: Executing work asynchronously via queues rather than synchronous request chains.
